name: FragmentViewer
intent: Renders a That Open Fragments (.frag) model with orbit, zoom and click-to-select — the same runtime the WC3 engineering viewers use. Fills its parent, reports the picked element, and releases its WebGL context on unmount.
when: Showing a single BIM/engineering model inside a product surface
Filling the canvas of a map/site workspace with a building rather than a basemap
A picked element must drive surrounding panels (selection is reported, not owned)
whenNot: Geospatial basemaps, geofences or asset pins -> use Map (mapbox-gl)
Whole-project federations of gigabyte scale -> stream through APS; Fragments loads one model into browser memory
IFC files -> convert to .frag first (IfcImporter); this widget deliberately avoids the 23 MB web-ifc wasm

chooseOver.component: Embedding a third-party BIM viewer in an iframe
chooseOver.because: FragmentViewer renders in-page, themes with the surrounding surface and reports selection back to React.

allowedPlacement: a parent with a bounded height (the canvas fills its container)
forbiddenPlacement: inside a scrolling container with auto height (the canvas collapses to zero)
more than a couple per page (each instance holds a WebGL context)
commonMistakes: Omitting workerUrl or passing a bare specifier — a bundled library cannot resolve @thatopen/fragments/worker to a runtime URL, so the model silently never loads
Mounting it in an auto-height parent, which gives the canvas zero height
Passing a new inline onSelectionChange identity expecting a reload — handlers are held in refs precisely so the WebGL context survives re-renders

extracted: canvas-owned scene / camera / OrbitControls / render loop
debounced fragments.update on camera move, forced on rest
click raycast to highlight + selection callback

notes: three and @thatopen/fragments are OPTIONAL peerDependencies — only apps importing this widget install them (~900 KB)
pin @thatopen/fragments to the version that authored the .frag files; the WC3 dataset catalog records 3.4.6
scope is one model: multi-model federation, geospatial placement, isolation and QTO are deliberately out
